precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 33:10
precepts.why:
Genesis 2:7 says “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground.” People talk about evolution, that man came up from primates and formed over time into what we know today; that is not true. Everything in Israel United in Christ is done to edify the nation, and what we say we prove out of the word of God. Ecclesiasticus 33:10 is the second witness: “And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.”

Some will ask how we know man was made from the dust, since that is not what the white man’s science says. Science is only good if it goes with the Bible; if it contradicts the Bible, we don't give a damn about science. But the honest science agrees. The infographic From Dust to Dust, the elements that connect us to Earth, shows that the human body is made mainly of elements also found in soil. The six main elements of life, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur, are in every cell, molecule and structure of the body and make up over 99 percent of our mass. The essential minerals, calcium for bones and teeth, potassium for the muscles and heart, magnesium, sodium and chlorine, are the same nutrients the soil gives the plants. The trace elements, iron for carrying oxygen, zinc for the immune system and healing, silicon and manganese, are in the soil too. We come from the earth, and to the earth we return, just like the Bible says.

The Most High is a mastermind, the author of beauty, the creator of all things, and he knew what he was doing when he pulled Adam from the dust of the ground. Our bodies are a testament that his word is true. The Bible is a true book, and we don't give a damn what anybody has to say about how our God, our father, created us. The teaching that man came from primates is there to contradict God’s word, because they know our God is a black man.

Paul says the same: “The first man is of the earth, earthy,” and “As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy.” Adam was earthy, and so are we; we come from the same soil as our father Adam, and “as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.” Meanwhile the other nations make sure we are deficient in these very things, and much of the food we eat diminishes them to kill us faster. So it is important, brothers and sisters, to keep a healthy diet.

precepts.label: Genesis 43:32
precepts.why:
“And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.” Our forefathers hated Joseph and sold him into slavery. He gained status in Egypt, Egypt got through the famine by his counsel, and now his brothers came to Egypt to buy food.

“And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.” If Joseph had been a German Jew, or from Holland, Ukraine or Poland, they would have known him: a white man in Egyptian clothes stands out among Egyptians, because the Egyptians are black. They could not recognize their brother because he was dressed in Egyptian garb, beard shaved, looking like an Egyptian. “for he spake unto them by an interpreter”: he acted the part, speaking Egyptian so they would not know him. Joseph passed for an African, a black man, just as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were dark ancestors.

Then Genesis 43:32, at the meal: “And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.” That is Jim Crow. The Hebrews sat over there and the Egyptians over here, because them sitting together was an abomination. Israel had its own land, Goshen, and Egypt was apart. It was still segregation, even though both were dark: same color, different nation.

The pictures shown from the history books said the same. The Egyptians are brown. The Israelites working in the granary under a taskmaster have afros. Pharaoh is black, and Tutankhamun is black. Nefertiti is black as hell, and the Nubians are black as hell. The sacrifice of Isaac in the mosaic of the Beth Alpha synagogue shows Abraham and Isaac as black. The sons of Ham, the Egyptians, Canaanites, Nubians and Libyans, are all dark; we fought the Canaanites in the land, and they are black too.

Moses passed for an Egyptian the same way. Jethro's daughters said, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. Moses married an Ethiopian woman, a daughter of Ham, and a Hamite would have known a white man was no Egyptian. Even Pharaoh's daughter knew the baby was a Hebrew only because he was circumcised, since both peoples were black.

precepts.label: Exodus 1:8
precepts.why:
“Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph”. This new king set taskmasters over Israel to afflict them with burdens, and then went further: “And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive”.

That is gator bait. They sacrificed our baby boys in the river to Sobek, the gator god. The white man did the exact same thing to us in the Florida Everglades: put our babies in a net, wait for the alligator to bite, pull the gator out and make shoes and bags out of him. Egypt did it to us first. They killed the males and kept the women alive, because the women do not produce the nation; the man does.

That decree is why Moses was hidden three months and laid in an ark of bulrushes by the river's brink, and why everything that follows was done in secret. When Pharaoh's daughter came down to the river in Exodus 2:5 and found the ark, she found one of the very sons her father had ordered cast into the river.

precepts.label: Numbers 12:1
precepts.why:
When Pharaoh's daughter opened the ark, “she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children”. How did she know? He was circumcised. You never read about Moses getting circumcised; he was already cut, because some of our forefathers retained that custom from our fathers. Outside of that, she would not have known the difference, because Egyptians and Hebrews were both black.

Then Moses fled to Midian and helped the seven daughters of the priest of Midian at the well, and they told their father Reuel, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. What did they call Moses? An Egyptian. The same way Joseph's brothers took Joseph for an Egyptian. Reuel, Jethro, gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

Numbers 12:1 shows what that family was: “And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman”. She was Ethiopian, so Moses' father-in-law was an Ethiopian, a priest of Midian but not a Midianite. Ethiopians are children of Ham, Kushites, the family of the Egyptians. A Hamite would know a Hamite when he saw one, and they still took Moses for an Egyptian. If he had been a white man, they would have known he was no Egyptian.

Paul passed for one too: “Art not thou that Egyptian”, the chief captain asked, and Paul answered, “I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus”. Moses passed for an Egyptian, Joseph passed for an Egyptian, Paul passed for an Egyptian. These are black people. That's the point.

precepts.why:
Leviticus 12:4 says “she shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purifying be fulfilled.” Purification means being washed, cleansed, made holy; literally, removing what is foreign and contaminated to restore something to its natural clean state. So purification is not just staying away from the temple. The days of her separation are also her being nursed back to health, restored.

Esther shows purification too. Go there and read it for yourselves: Esther went through her days of purification with sweet odours and so forth, and everything else she needed, and she had maids to help her. It is a different purification, but it shows that purifying a woman is a lot of stuff: care, help, the right food, the things her body needs.

So it is with a woman after she gives birth. She was not just sent home and left alone. For those forty days, or eighty for a girl, she was kept in a special place, and midwives and family came, cooked the right food and nursed her back to health. That is postpartum in the Bible, and it is why a sister who has just given birth needs people around her and help with the baby, not the postpartum depression that Esau made up.

precepts.label: Lamentations 5:11
precepts.why:
“They ravished the women in Zion, and the maids in the cities of Judah.” They raped our women; they raped the Judahite sisters. This is not new. Whatever color the oppressor was, the nations all had the same habits, because judgment is like a ring: it recurs over and over again. Same game, different characters.

It is the curse of Deuteronomy 28:30: “Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her”. In The Butler, the master takes the boy's mother from the cotton field; she cannot say no; she screams, and the father and everyone in the field stand there powerless, unable to do a thing. In The Birth of a Nation, a guest demands Hark's new wife Esther for the night, and the master allows it; she comes out in tears, and he cries, Where is God now? That racial anger is what drove Nat Turner to take the axe to the master. We were powerless to protect our wives and our children. And “thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein”: we built the house and never dwelt in it.

That trauma is the madness of verse 28: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart”. Coming off those ships we were smitten with madness. In 12 Years a Slave, Patsey, beaten until her back was ripped open for a piece of soap because she could not stand her own smell, begs Solomon Northup to hold her under the water until she is without life, and to bury her in a lonely place; she has no comfort in this life. You cannot expect reparations to fix that. Blindness is spiritual: some watching right now say Jesus and the Jews are white; they are gone. “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways”, as a nation.

You millennials grew up thinking the white man is peaceful and loving and your friend. Malcolm X, Martin Luther King and our people of the 50s, 60s and 70s knew who the enemy was; after that we forgot and started saying the enemy is only a spiritual demon. They gave us Section 8, food stamps and Christianity, and we went back to sleep. So God is letting Trump and the administration behind him do evil, reverting the white man to his true nature, and JD Vance says they will no longer apologize for being white, so that we develop that racial anger again. That is why they want to remove this history from the museums and the schools. Let your children watch Roots, 12 Years a Slave, The Birth of a Nation, Amistad; the Holy Ghost brings all things to remembrance, and the scripture says what they did to our women in Zion.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:32
precepts.why:
“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”: in chattel slavery our lives were in doubt every day. Every day there was a chance we would be killed, a chance we might get lynched. And not only the lives of the mothers and fathers were in doubt; our sons were in doubt too. That is why verse 32 is read here: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people.”

That could have happened at any moment, any day. Your son ripped out of your arms to be sold to Master so-and-so, and you would never see your children again. From the day that child was born until the day someone said, I want that one as a slave, the parents lived with it, and they had nothing to say about it. “and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long”: they watched their sons get taken away and watched their daughters get taken away. That is the failing of eyes and the sorrow of mind of verse 65: no way to change your reality, no future you can see for your children.

“and there shall be no might in thine hand”: no might in our hands to stop it. And there was no alcohol for them. A bottle of whiskey would not have stopped that. They had to endure this thing sober, knowing the Lord was still going to be with us somehow, some way. So they could not off themselves, because a generation was going to come from them, from the wife and from the husband, and our seed would continue while they went through trauma after trauma.

It took faith to make it from morning to night and night to morning, and they did not even have the truth the way we know it today. They pushed through all that evil and ugliness so that you and I could sit here today. So what excuse do we have? We cannot leave our post to drink and get high, or put our head inside a bottle and a crack pipe, when our forefathers endured this and kept pushing.

precepts.label: Lamentations 5:12
precepts.why:
“Princes are hanged up by their hand: the faces of elders were not honoured.” Princes hanged up means lynched. Young or old, it did not matter; you were hanged all the same.

That is what “thy life shall hang in doubt before thee” comes to. Hanging in doubt does mean you will wonder whether you live or die, worried day and night, in the hood, the ghetto and the slums, and further back in slavery and colonization: “In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning!” But it also means hanging. Lamentations 5 is the whole picture of the curse: “Our inheritance is turned to strangers, our houses to aliens”, the European, the East Indian and the Chinese man in Africa and Trinidad reaping our resources; “We have drunken our water for money; our wood is sold unto us”, which is colonization; “Servants have ruled over us”, those who were once our slaves.

The Spaniards hanged the Americans thirteen at a time and set them on fire. Without Sanctuary, a book of lynching photographs, shows it: 1935, which was yesterday; postcards of our fore mothers and fathers hanging from trees; a man burned to pieces, his hands and legs cut off and kept as souvenirs; a mother and son hanged from a bridge in 1901. White people today say, I didn't do that, that was my ancestors. But look at the postcards: children, fathers, mothers, women right in the middle, the whole family supporting it, children who grew up to be your lawyers, teachers, mayors and police officers.

Mary Turner, in 1918, grieving her husband Hayes Turner, lynched without a trial, threatened to have his killers punished. The next day she was hanged from a tree, burned, her womb cut open; the baby, a month shy of being born, cried on the ground, and a member of the white mob crushed its head with his foot; then they shot her full of holes. Now they say they are not apologizing anymore. In Queens in 1976 white children chased little black girls out of their neighborhood with rocks and dogs, calling them niggers, and those children are judges, lawyers and police officers now. This is war.

Hanging is nothing new; the Persians did it (1 Esdras 6:32), “out of his own house should a tree be taken, and he thereon be hanged”. Christ himself was lynched: “whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” Peter called the cross a tree, wood, where he hung for hours. “Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”: Christ went under the curse along with us. The King and his children were hanged. Princes are hanged up by their hand.

The Greeks did it too. Under Antiochus, 1 Maccabees 1:60-61: “they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised.” “And they hanged the infants about their necks, and rifled their houses, and slew them that had circumcised them.” After they killed the mothers, they hung the circumcised babies from their dead mothers' necks and put them on display for the people to see. They lynched our babies on their mothers' necks. It is the same persecution recorded of the mothers who circumcised their children and were led about the city with the babes at their breasts.

Esau was so demonic and wicked that he ran around checking who was circumcised, running through our houses and killing anyone who circumcised a child. Who does that? Demons.

That is Deuteronomy 28:66: “thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”. Keeping the law of God, circumcising your child as the covenant commands, could cost a mother her life and her baby's. It is the same spirit that hanged our princes, burned our mothers and crushed our babies here in America. Same game, different characters: judgment is like a ring, recurring over and over.

Peter and the apostles answered, “We ought to obey God rather than men”, and the mothers of the Maccabees did so to the death. Christ was hanged on a tree too; the King and his children have all hung under the same curse, until the Lord says enough.

precepts.label: Psalms 137:3
precepts.why:
“For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.” “How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a strange land?” We read it right there in the history of the slave ships.

Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. What does Egypt represent? “I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.” Egypt is bondage. The Lord would bring us into bondage again, this time by way of ships; literal Egypt we would see no more again as a nation, and there we would be sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, slave men and slave women.

The Middle Passage, the Maafa, a massive disaster: for fifty days or more our people were packed in spaces as tight as coffins, a second platform barely twenty inches above the heads of those below, chained to the floor, lying in their own waste, amid rats that gnawed through wood and flesh, on floors covered with blood and excrement, where pregnant women gave birth and the living awoke chained to the dead. Tight packers crammed in as many as possible, reckoning the sales would offset the dead. The meal was horse beans pounded to a pulp with slabber sauce, once or twice a day, and a pint of water. Dumb negroes say it never happened and ask where the ships are: cargo ships carried spices and corn before us, carried us as cargo, and after slavery carried cargo again. Why get rid of them?

Then came the dancing of the slaves: the crew played the bagpipe or forced our ancestors to beat out a rhythm while they jumped about, ankles rubbed raw by the leg irons, to keep the human cargo in salable condition. That is Psalms 137:3: those who carried us away captive required of us mirth. At night the cries rose; an enslaved woman explained the howling came from having dreamt they were in their own country and waking in the hold of a slave ship. A strange land indeed.

Millions were carried from Africa to the West Indies, North and South America and Europe, from Luanda, from the Congo, from Loango, where the old maps mark the Jews; the buyers and sellers both knew they were selling outsiders, not the same people. Deuteronomy 28:68 and Psalms 137:3 were fulfilled on those ships.

precepts.label: John 3:3
precepts.why:
A lot of us are not finding comfort in the scriptures because we lack faith. You don’t believe the Bible can transform you. You don’t believe it can turn you into another man, that you could become a whole different person. But 1 Samuel 10:6 says it: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

John 3:3 says the same thing to Nicodemus: “Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

Being turned into another man is being born again. The brother who drank a whole fifth in one night, the one who says, I can’t put it down, it’s a part of me, is not stuck being that man. Except he be born again, turned into another man, he cannot see the kingdom. The bottle is the battle, and the Bible is how you are turned into another man and win it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:34
precepts.why:
1 Samuel 10:6 says you “shalt be turned into another man.” 2 Esdras 14:34 tells you what your part is in that turning.

“Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.”

Subdue your own understanding and reform your heart. We have to be transformed in the renewing of our minds. Transformed.

That is what the brother with the addiction runs from. He comes to the table having drunk a whole fifth in one night and says he is not an alcoholic. Even the white man knows the first step of recovery is to admit it: you have to realize you need help, that you are sick. Has he watched the classes on alcohol the Bishops and Deacons go over all the time? No. Why not? Because he is running away from his issues, and you cannot run away from that thing. You have to subdue your own understanding, reform your heart, and let the word turn you into another man, and then you shall be kept alive and after death obtain mercy.

precepts.label: Galatians 6:1
precepts.why:
Eliphaz says to Job, “Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” A lot of brothers go out and teach, some at camp 30 days in a row, 100 days, 365 days. We strengthen the weak hands: people come into the body sick and needing help, marriages come in messed up, and we dedicate our time to figuring out how to fix them.

That is Galatians 6:1: “Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.” Brothers will fall, sisters will fall, people in the congregation will fall, and we spend a lot of our time restoring them, bringing them back up, getting them back in position and making them better than they used to be. We do it for everybody else.

As a leader in this truth your phone rings all day: can I counsel with you, I've got a question. We answer, we deal with it, and when we don't know the answer we go to leadership and get counsel for their counsel. “Thy words have upholden him that was falling”: put the cigarettes down, bro; stop smoking weed; see, the Bible says this.

But the verse says, “considering thyself”. Inside our own household we don't do it. Our wife asks a question and we say, go watch 15 minutes with the captains. We deal with everything on the outside, but we are not teaching and building up our own possession. So when it comes upon us, “thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.” You freeze up, you fold up, and you go against your own counsel, because most men don't counsel about what is going on in their own household. The one who restores everybody else has to consider himself too.

precepts.label: Sirach 6:17-18
precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.” The law of God is perfect, it is pure, there is nothing wrong with it, and converting means to change. Only the law can change you. I used to be a murderer; the law said thou shalt not murder. I used to be a thief; the law said thou shalt not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I know the Lord, I repent. Same thing, brother. Same thing, sister, with your trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. It happened when you were 14, 15, 16, and now you're 46, 50, in your third marriage, still using it, and you can't keep a man or a woman because you cannot cope.

We never grew up around order, structure and unity. So when we come around it now, we begin to feel uncomfortable, because we realize we are the problem: the reason environments become toxic, the reason people bicker and fight, the instigating spirit we grew up seeing. Now, in a body and a truth where the light shines on that, you are forced to change, and brothers and sisters do not want to.

“Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.” If you fear the Lord, you are going to direct your friendships aright, because as you are, so shall your neighbour be. But if you are constantly having issues, constantly having problems, who is the issue? Who is causing these troubles? With the laws of God and all the examples in the scriptures, you should be able to direct your friendship aright. So why is your name always in something?

“My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age.” We didn't have the opportunity to gather instruction from our youth up. But coming into this truth we have to be born again and begin to do so. You can't drag in all the ways your grandmama and your auntie and them used to deal with each other. It's a new day.

precepts.label: Sirach 6:20-21
precepts.why:
“She is very unpleasant to the unlearned.” Wisdom is very unpleasant to the unlearned. You didn't learn about yourself. All you ever did was point out other people's problems. You never examined yourself; you never looked in the mirror. So now that wisdom finally reveals who you are, it is very unpleasant.

“he that is without understanding will not remain with her.” That's why people have to find a reason to leave. They get offended, they find a reason to be mad, and then they go. What is the root cause? They don't want to change once that wisdom is revealed. And the law, which is perfect, converts only the soul that will be changed.

Destructive attitudes begin internally before they become visible externally. A person may still attend services, teach, lead, pray or serve while harboring the wrong spirit, an evil spirit. You look at the fringes and think, he's good, she's good; you would be surprised how many have an evil spirit in the midst of us. Some come here to destroy the unity of the brotherhood, because in the world it's always chaos: you never see a room full of black people with no fight, no argument, breaking bread together. Whatever you were going through in the world, you had better get over it, and quick, because that thing will destroy you. Those who carry that spirit will find themselves outside these doors.

precepts.label: Matthew 11:28
precepts.why:
The bottle says, forget your pain; the Bible says, “Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee.” The bottle says, numb your sorrow. Christ answers that lie: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.”

The bottle offers to carry your burden for you. It talks to you like scripture in a dark room with one light over the table: drink me, I can take away thy sorrows; you're depressed, don't worry about it; you're stressed out, put the kids to bed early and drink me. That is a spirit having a conversation with you.

Christ is the one who actually takes the weight. The labouring and heavy laden are told to come to him, not to the liquor store, and he gives rest. The bottle only numbs the sorrow until tomorrow; casting the burden on the Lord is how he sustains you and keeps the righteous from being moved.

precepts.label: Romans 8:1
precepts.why:
The bottle says, you are a failure. You ain't nothing. You're going to be the same person you always were. The Bible says: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.”

Guess what? You can repent. The bottle says you're a failure; the Bible says you can repent and become a new man.

But it starts with acknowledging it: I'm an alcoholic. I'm a fornicator, an adulterer, a liar, a thief; I deal with envy, covetousness, idolatry. That is where the change happens. And acknowledging it is not enough; you have to work on fixing those things. You can't say, I'm an alcoholic, and keep going out drinking.

No condemnation belongs to those who walk after the Spirit and not after the flesh. The man chained to the bottle is walking after the flesh; the man who casts his burden on the Lord and walks in the Spirit is free of the condemnation the bottle keeps whispering over him.

precepts.label: Psalms 19:7
precepts.why:
The bottle says, you can't change. You're the same; you're going to be that same person. The Bible says, “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul.”

The law of the Lord converts the soul: it changes a man. So the lie that you can't change is answered by the perfect law of God. You can repent and become a new man.

That is the other side of casting your burden on the Lord. You don't just hand him the weight; you take on his law, and his law turns you into somebody different. The bottle keeps you drunk and stupid, the way the enemy wants it, with a liquor store in every black neighborhood and weed stores everywhere to keep you high, drunk and stupid. The law of the Lord makes the simple wise and converts the soul out of that.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:18
precepts.why:
The bottle says, take another drink. You can handle it; drink some more. The Bible says, “And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.”

The bottle wants to fill you: drink me and be filled with my love. It says, you're alone, nobody understands us, I love you more than anybody. I love you more than water. You don't need to eat today; I'll make the food taste better. You can't sleep; I can put you to sleep so fast you won't even realize it. The bottle starts talking like scripture: I am that I am, the comfort of them all.

That is excess, and it destroys the body too. Alcohol builds fat around your organs and your belly, raises your risk of heart disease, high blood pressure and type two diabetes, makes you hungrier and drives you to fast food. Four or five shots a drink every day is thousands of calories a week, and then you wonder why you can't lose weight or climb a flight of stairs.

The command is to be filled with something else: the Spirit. Cast your burden on the Lord and be filled with his Spirit, not with the bottle.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:12-13
precepts.why:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”. The book of the Lord is no other book on this planet except the Bible. Solomon warns: “And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.”

Anything outside of the Bible that you try to live your life by is a weariness of the flesh. All you will profit from it is getting tired. You might get a good night's sleep, unless a demon flies out of the bag reading some book with some kind of skin on it. There is no end to these books: they are always writing some book about what God is going to do on this earth, about his plans and who his people are. No other book can answer that except the Bible. The much study of the rest of these books is a waste of time.

When books are brought in class, they are filtered through the Bible. If they contradict the Bible, if they go against the laws, the commandments and the prophecies, they are garbage. They are brought only to illuminate the reading, as in Nehemiah 8:8.

“Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter”: the conclusion of the whole matter is in the Bible. Daniel says the same: “Hitherto is the end of the matter”, the kingdom given to the people of the saints of the Most High. “Fear God, and keep his commandments”: his commandments are found in the book of the Lord, not in the Quran, not in the Egyptian book of the dead. That is how you know which is the book of the Lord.

“for this is the whole duty of man.” The image of God is doing what God said. The man spoken of is the Israelite man, because we are the ones who will make everybody else dance to the tune of this Bible, but it has to be done by us first. We are in training. That is why we are on this slave ship called America: because we broke God's laws and his commandments, and we must endure all of it to get back home.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 8:8
precepts.why:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”. The Bible alone is the book of the Lord, so why are other books ever brought into the class? Because of Nehemiah: “So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.”

Whatever is brought before the brothers and sisters is brought by the commandments of God, to illuminate the reading and make sense of it: to give the sense and cause them to understand. Sometimes tangible things, relative to your understanding today, are grabbed to help you see what is written in the Bible better. That is the only reason books are referenced here and there.

But everything is filtered through the Bible. If a book contradicts the Bible, if it goes against the laws, the commandments and the prophecies, it is garbage and is not dealt with at all. None of these books can be mated to the Bible. The Bible stands alone, and the other books only serve to give the sense of it.

precepts.label: Job 36:15

Isaiah 61:1 says the Lord “hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted”. We are the brokenhearted. We are the ones crying out in the streets, to this day. And Job shows what the Lord does with us in that condition: “He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.”

The Lord is telling you there is going to be so much oppression going on that you are going to have to listen to the word of God. The Carmelo Anthony situation, that's oppression: he is in the prison house for defending himself. And the same week of his verdict, a baby was shot dead in Mississippi. These things are going to continue to happen.

Oppression, persecution, tribulation, all these things are going to arise for God's people to realize who they are. That is how he opens our ears. And yet some want to leave the truth because they got called fat, or because they got demoted. That is some evil stuff: traitors and betrayers.

So Isaiah 61 is proclaimed to the ones whose ears the oppression has opened: liberty to the captives, “the opening of the prison to them that are bound”, because we are yet this day in captivity and we fill the prison houses. What is there to hope for outside of the body of Christ? Only the ones who know who they are can look for “the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God”.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 2:10
precepts.why:
The Lord has set watchmen upon the walls of Jerusalem “which shall never hold their peace day nor night”. Watchmen pay attention to the condition of the people and to the enemy coming to destroy the people. “ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence, And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.”

Nehemiah shows how the enemy takes it when Israel speaks up: “When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.” They do not like it when we speak up for our people.

That is why our enemies want us silent, locked away with the key thrown away and our mouths zipped. They call us troublemakers. Yes, we are causing trouble, because you are not supposed to be over us. They want a quiet slave.

The squeaky wheel gets the oil. Quiet people are ignored, and noisy people force others to take action. So we will complain, judge, bring out the records and tell it like it is, and we will beg the Lord and give him no rest, like the widow before the unjust judge, until he kills our enemies and sets Jerusalem up on high.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 17:12
precepts.why:
“For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.” Succours means comforts. Fear is a betraying comfort.

We are encouraged to be sports figures, entertainers and dancers, to frolic: to play, jump and move about in a happy, lively, carefree way, and never think about anything serious, because then we become a danger. Frolic produces an image of comfort that is false. The athlete makes millions running up and down the court and thinks he has made it, but the real soul of him knows he is still a slave. Keeping us in the silly mode makes us consumers, not people who run our own banks and medical centers.

Kaepernick caught the fever. He looked at what was happening to his people while he was up there throwing the ball, got serious and stood up, and you saw how they dealt with him. His teammates know he did the right thing, but they have to pretend they are all right. That pretending is the fear: they stay in that mess and never stand up to be men, lying to themselves that they are comfortable being clowns.

So the watchmen of Isaiah 62 cannot hold their peace. We cannot drown out the horrible squeaking of our wretched condition, the psychological traumas we live through, with frolic, drugs, alcohol or music. We cannot be dancing slaves made to look whole while inside there is a spiritual rot we can no longer afford. We must stand up and be real men and women, keep not silence, and give the Lord no rest.

precepts.label: Romans 7:15
precepts.why:
The foundational question is: am I who I was created to be, or am I what I was conditioned to become? It is not a surface-level question; it is an identity question that deals with the real soul of man and woman. Everything about us, our patterns, our responses, our beliefs, our defenses, has been shaped by one of two forces: creation or conditioning. Creation speaks to design; conditioning speaks to experience. One is intentional, the other reactive. One reflects origin, the image God made; the other reflects adaptation, to slavery, to ghettos, to being taken advantage of, to being unclean, a gang member, a drug addict. That is not who we really are, and most people live somewhere in between without ever telling the two apart.

Paul shows that fight in Romans 7:15: “For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.” What he ends up doing, the real him does not allow. What his spirit would do, the conditioned self will not follow. And what the real him hates, the righteous part connected to God that hates evil, he does anyway, acting from conditioning and not from what the Lord made him to be. “If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.” That duality goes on with us every day.

Christ said you must deny yourself. The you that does the denying is the part God is dealing with; the self is the composite of the conditioning you were made into. So examine your own thoughts and behaviors and ask: why am I behaving like this? Is this the real me, or a response to what I have been conditioned to be?

Most of the time when we deal with our people, we are dealing with the mask, the representative, like the man holding up a sign in front of himself. The real soul is buried and scared, hiding under a tarp of trauma, lies, deceit and psychological hang-ups. The greatness buried under self-doubt has not surfaced yet. That is what is meant by the Negro being made in a lab: the real him has not stood up. We have to encourage that real spirit to come forward and be the image God made.

precepts.label: Genesis 1:27-28
precepts.why:
You were created with intention: not randomly formed, not accidentally designed, not undefined in purpose. You have a purpose; you just lost your way. “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” Replenish the earth means have babies.

This is the original declaration, not only about humanity in general but about you specifically, the real soul of man and woman. Not the whore, the drug addict, the drug dealer they told you that you are. The real you is about righteousness, and you cannot define yourself by the conditioning of how you have been made to look. Conditioning says, we want to make a slave out of him, out of her, and make them think that is what they innately are. That is the point of saying the Negro was created in a lab: the real him has not stood up yet, the real us has not even surfaced yet.

You were made in the image of God, not in the image of your dysfunction. Not the image of your traumatic experiences, even though we have been through all kinds of trauma. Not the image crafted by an unstable childhood, an abusive relationship, or an environment that never reflected your worth back to you. Where it was said that we are not his people, it shall be said that we are the sons and daughters of God. We are not what they say we are; we are what God said we are. Carry yourselves that way and teach it to your children, because this world will turn them upside down if you are not serious about it.

Before conditioning entered, before survival strategies developed, before the false self was built, there was an image, an original design, and that design carries attributes: the capacity for creativity, for dominion, the capacity to rule, and for fruitfulness, children and nationhood. These are not just aspirations, like a novel we read. They are original; they are in our DNA, placed in us before the world opened its lips to say anything. When people see what we build and say it must be a sellout, that is a dysfunctional mind that believes we can't do anything. Men and women, whatever you went through, you can fix it. In IUIC we told everyone who said we couldn't to go to hell, and we did what we had to do.

precepts.label: Exodus 11:7
precepts.why:
The attributes of the image were placed in us before the world had its say, and Exodus 11:7 shows how God guards his people: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

Are we the children of Israel? Then not a dog shall open its lips against us. No one can talk against us or anything that belongs to us. The Lord put a difference so that the world may know. We are his holy jewels, the jewellery God will wear around his neck, the apple of his eye. When they speak against us, they are speaking against his jewels and his people.

Carry yourselves like that, and never mind people who say you can't boast. Even in captivity: it is only temporary. We are not the finished product of what they did to us. A day is coming when this will be gone, and everything that ever spoke against our people will face judgment. They say, you don't talk like a slave. That is because we are not slaves.

Be like Christ. On the cross, he knew he could call down legions to wipe them out in the blink of an eye, because he already had the power, and he says we will be joint heirs with him. The world is scared to death that we will ever make that connection. They do not want us connected to that kind of power.

precepts.label: Isaiah 43:21
precepts.why:
“This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.” This people is the Israelites, Judah: God formed us for himself, to show forth his praise, and all the other nations will catch hell.

Put that in your spirit and put it in your children's spirit. Teach your children they are superior, because they are. The world tells us lies: it shows us Superman and Batman and all kinds of fools on TV and makes us think we are nothing but criminals. Then, when we say the reverse, they try the Jedi mind trick and make us think we are doing something wrong. That is why sons need fathers in the household who think this way, so they grow up in the right posture.

We were not formed for survival or to be a product of our environment. We were formed for a purpose that comes from outside our circumstances, connected to the nature and intent of the Most High who formed us. That is Jeremiah 1:5: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Before the sperm hit the egg, we already existed and were known by him, and he chose which spirit to send, this one rather than that one, for a purpose. “and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations”: whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be. He made us the children of Israel and put talents in us. That is why those talents must be organized and not wasted. Don't bring self-doubt; get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

precepts.label: Lamentations 5:10
precepts.why:
Lamentations 4:7 shows Israel before: “Her Nazarites were purer than snow, they were whiter than milk”. Whiter means holier, more righteous. “more ruddy in body than rubies”: ruddy in body means healthy in body, strong and precious. Then Babylon came, cut off the food supply and starved them out. Verse 7 is the before and verse 8 is the after: “Their visage is blacker than a coal; they are not known in the streets: their skin cleaveth to their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick.” Their faces could not be recognised from verse 7; they went from ruddy in body to skin hanging off their bones.

Lamentations 5:10 says it plainly: “Our skin was black like an oven because of the terrible famine.” What caused the famine? The Babylonians surrounded us, besieged us, cut off our food and water supply, and starved us for years before conquering us entirely. Through starvation we got darker, blacker than a coal.

“Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.” From here on out, you are not going to say, well, my daddy was wicked, so I am just going to be wicked by default. No, you are going to change it.

“neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son: the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.” Each soul answers for itself.

precepts.label: Acts 5:30
precepts.why:
Peter and the other apostles told our wicked elders, “We ought to obey God rather than men.” And then: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” Christ was lynched.

Why does Peter call it a tree? What is the cross made of? Wood. Hanging on the cross is hanging on a tree. He says it again in Acts 10:39: “whom they slew and hanged on a tree”. Some say he was hanged from an actual tree, but Thomas said, “Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.” What would they need nails for on a tree? His hands and feet were nailed to a cross, and he hung there for hours, lynched slowly. And they mocked him: “If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.” A man hanging by the neck from a tree could not be answering questions; he would be choking to death. So Peter called the crucifixion hanging on a tree, and the two men beside him were lynched too.

It is ironic: the same way the white man lynched us in slavery and into the 60s is the same way our King was killed. That is why Galatians 3:13 matters: “Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. Christ was hanged on a tree under the same curse as his people.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 21:23
precepts.why:
Hanging was our punishment too, in the law, for the wicked: “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree:” “His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled”.

That is what Paul quotes in Galatians 3:13: “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. The curse of the law means its condemnation; being made a curse means being put to death for us, a sacrifice.

So what happened to our people? We were hanged on trees, because we went under the curses. Christ went under the curses of Deuteronomy 28 along with us, and we are under the curses too. He that is hanged is accursed of God: Christ was hanged on a tree, and so were we. The King and his children were hanged.

And the pattern keeps turning, like a ring. In Egypt, when Moses said, let my people go to serve God, Pharaoh called us idle and took away the straw but kept the tale of bricks, with a quota of 2,000 bricks; the records name Yupa son of Uriah, a Hebrew, 370 short. Here it was a quota of 200 or 500 pounds of cotton. The officers set over us, the black elites, pastors and politicians in the white man's pocket, turned on Moses and Aaron for making Pharaoh hate them. It is the same curse, the same judgment, until Christ, who bore the curse, redeems us from it.
